title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Page 4 of a short sequence (pp. 131-133) in which Grothendieck works out what a morphism between 'ateliers' should be. An atelier 𝒜 is a set of 'elementary figures' (Figel) of a space E. It carries three relations, written ◁ (inclusion-type), ∘≪ (a strict, interior-type inclusion) and |∘| (a disjointness- or position-type relation). Passing to 'sommets' (vertices) produces Boolean-type operations Sup, Inf and complement ∁.

The previous page treated two cases.
- Case 2°: a map f: E'→E with pullback f*: Figures(E)→Figures(E'). If f is not surjective, f* sends 𝒜 into 𝒜'∪{∅}, where ∅ is the empty figure. f* is compatible with ◁, ∘≪ and |∘| but in general not injective.
- Case 3°: an injective map g: E→E' with direct image g_*: 𝒜→𝒜', also injective.

This page unifies the two. A correspondence (span) E ←f− Γ −f'→ E' with f': Γ→E' injective gives the composite f'_* ∘ f*: 𝒜 → 𝒜'∪{∅}. Such a span is just a partial map E' ⇀ E defined on Γ ⊂ E', so this is pullback of figures along a partial map. It is compatible with the three relations, and cases 2° and 3° are the special cases where one leg is the identity.

Grothendieck then notes that for a non-injective g: E→E' there seems to be no direct way to transport figures. Direct images of elementary figures do not preserve the disjointness and inclusion data.

He concludes that for a general morphism of ateliers one must find what replaces such a 'correspondence', without the set-theoretic operations. This leads to conditions (α_i, β_i?). The next page carries this out: a provisional homomorphism is a map 𝒜 → 𝒜'⊔{∅} preserving ◁, ∘≪ and |∘|, with conventions for ∅.

The rotated marginal note appears to check, in cases 2° and 3°, that elementary figures are sent to elementary figures or to ∅. It may involve a condition like #(A)=1 (singleton or connectedness?). It is largely illegible.
errors: The notation switches between pages. On the previous page f: E'→E and g: E→E'; here f: Γ→E and f': Γ→E' with f' injective. These are consistent once the span is read as a partial map E' ⇀ E.
Compatibility of f'_*∘f* with ∁ fails in general, as already stated on the previous page. This page does not restate it.

ideas.what: A span E ← Γ ↪ E' with injective leg, i.e. a partial map E' ⇀ E, acts on elementary figures as a map 𝒜 → 𝒜'∪{∅} unifying pullback and injective push-forward.
ideas.modern_name: Contravariant action of partial maps on subsets / pointed maps (Kleisli category of the 'maybe' monad)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (partial-map categories; e.g. Robinson–Rosolini 1988 for categories of partial maps)
ideas.where_published: Unpublished 1986 'ateliers' notes (cote 156-9); not in EGA/SGA/Esquisse as far as known

ideas.what: Observation that a non-injective map gives no direct transport of figures. Hence a general atelier morphism must be defined abstractly, without set-theoretic operations.
ideas.modern_name: Morphisms of relational/proximity structures defined intrinsically (cf. de Vries algebra morphisms, contact algebra morphisms)

missed.claim: The atelier structure resembles structures studied in point-free topology and mereotopology. Its relations ◁ (part-of), ∘≪ (well-inside / non-tangential part) and |∘| (disjointness) parallel de Vries proximity algebras, contact algebras and RCC relations. The partial-map style morphisms (into 𝒜'⊔{∅}) parallel those structures' morphism notions. Grothendieck's 1986 ateliers do not appear to have been compared with that literature.
missed.quote: Dans le cas d'une [morphisme?] d'atelier quelconque, il faut une ... "correspondance" ... les opérations
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This would place Grothendieck's late 'ateliers' (tame-topology foundations) within existing point-free and mereotopological frameworks, and could clarify which of his axioms are new.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine step: it unifies pullback and injective push-forward via spans with a mono leg, i.e. partial maps. Its only interest is as part of the little-known atelier project and its plausible kinship with proximity/contact algebras.
transcription_corrections: 'une semble pas y avoir' should read 'Il ne semble pas y avoir d'application directe des figures, pour une application g: E→E' qui ne soit pas injective.'

'Dans le cas d'une multiplication d'atelier quelconque' is more likely 'Dans le cas d'un morphisme(?) d'ateliers quelconque', followed by '...qui se substitue(?) type aux "correspondances" ... sans les opérations ensemblistes(?) – d'où une ... α_i, β_i'.
Line 3 likely reads 'Γ → E' soit injectif. Dans ce cas [on retrouve] 2° et 3° (en fait, une des deux)... [application] 𝒜 → 𝒜'∪{∅}.'
